name: Morphine
status: PILOT – † lines checked against a UK product summary (SA package insert could not be opened) 2026-11-15; awaiting review

pi_source.title: Morphine sulfate 10 / 15 / 30 mg/mL solution for injection – UK Summary of Product Characteristics (emc). NOT the South African package insert.

dagger_note: † = general pharmacology; not in the SA guideline and not stated in the product summary consulted
item_format: t=text, s=source:printed page (s=pi: product summary), d=dagger, n=from own notes, b=bold, h=heading
summary: Reference strong opioid for severe acute pain, labour and procedural analgesia, post-intubation sedation and palliative pain or dyspnoea.

forms.t: Oral solution (mist morphine); slow-release tablets 10 mg, 30 mg, 60 mg

moa.t: Full agonist at μ-opioid receptors: binds and imitates endogenous opioids
Effects: analgesia, sedation, dysphoria or euphoria, miosis
Acts mainly on the central nervous system and smooth muscle

pk.t: Children, IV: time to peak action 20–40 minutes; duration 4–6 hours
Metabolised mainly by glucuronidation to morphine-3- and morphine-6-glucuronide; about 90% excreted in urine within 24 hours; half-life 2–3 hours
The active metabolite morphine-6-glucuronide accumulates in renal failure

items.t: 3–5 mg IV as a single dose, then further boluses every 5–10 minutes, to a total maximum of 10 mg; repeat after 4 hours if necessary
Ward alternative: 1 mg IV boluses every 6–10 minutes, max 0.1–0.2 mg/kg 4 hourly
0.1–0.2 mg/kg IM 4 hourly (PHC: 5–10 mg IM 4–6 hourly when required)
0.1 mg/kg IM 4 hourly as needed, max 10 mg per dose
Before manual vacuum aspiration: 0.1 mg/kg IM 30 minutes before the procedure, max 10 mg
4-hourly IV bolus: neonate 0.025–0.05 mg/kg; 1–6 months 0.05 mg/kg; 6 months–1 year 0.05–0.2 mg/kg; 1–12 years 0.1–0.2 mg/kg
Infusion: neonate 5–10 mcg/kg/hour; 1–6 months 10–30 mcg/kg/hour; 6 months–12 years 20–30 mcg/kg/hour
Titrate in small doses at 5–10 minute intervals with frequent reassessment; give each bolus slowly over 3–5 minutes
IV: < 6 months 0.025–0.1 mg/kg/dose; ≥ 6 months 0.05–0.2 mg/kg/dose; repeat after 4 hours if required
Oral onset 20–40 minutes; peak 60–90 minutes; duration 3–6 hours
Solution: start 5–10 mg (max 0.2 mg/kg) 4 hourly; elderly or frail 2.5–5 mg (max 0.1 mg/kg) 4 hourly; titrate to effect
Slow-release tablets 12 hourly once the daily requirement is known
Oral 2.5–5 mg 4 hourly as required, titrate up slowly; renal failure: start 1–2 mg

administration.t: IV bolus: dilute 10 mg up to 10 mL with sodium chloride 0.9% (= 1 mg/mL)
Paediatric infusion: 0.5 mg/kg diluted up to 50 mL with dextrose 5% or sodium chloride 0.9%; 1 mL = 10 mcg/kg

adjustments.t: Reduce the dose in moderate to severe impairment; severe and prolonged respiratory depression has occurred
Palliative oral dosing in renal failure: start 1–2 mg and observe closely
Use with caution; consider dose reduction
Crosses the placenta rapidly; may cause respiratory depression in the newborn and reduce uterine contractions
A single dose appears compatible with breastfeeding; observe the infant with repeated doses

contraindications.t: Head injury, raised intracranial pressure, cerebral oedema
Obstructive airways disease; acute asthma attack
Monoamine oxidase inhibitors, or within 2 weeks of stopping them
Paralytic ileus, biliary colic, acute alcohol intoxication, phaeochromocytoma, convulsive disorders

cautions.t: Hypotension / hypovolaemia: in obstetric haemorrhage titrate only once systolic BP > 100 mmHg
Hypotension, reduced respiratory reserve, sleep apnoea, obesity: use reduced doses
Benzodiazepines and other sedatives: risk of sedation, respiratory depression, coma and death; alcohol adds to sedation and hypotension
Causes spasm of the sphincter of Oddi – avoid in biliary disorders
Dependence and tolerance with repeated use

adverse_effects.t: Very common: drowsiness, respiratory depression, constipation, nausea, vomiting, pruritus, sweating, confusion
Common: hypotension, bradycardia, miosis, urinary retention, dry mouth, bronchospasm, rash

monitoring.t: Monitor response to pain and effects on respiration and blood pressure
Recovery room / IV titration: conscious level and pulse oximetry continuously

toxicity.t: Overdose: respiratory depression, pinpoint pupils, coma, hypotension, hypothermia
Treatment: respiratory and cardiovascular support, and naloxone – see the Opioids pathway for the dose

conflicts.t: Labour: the product summary advises against morphine in pregnancy and labour; the STG and maternity guideline use it for labour analgesia. The pathway follows the STG.
Biliary colic and head injury are listed as contraindications in the product summary; check any pathway that gives morphine in these settings (e.g. cholecystitis).
